title: African flower hexagon variant
subtitle: Pointed hexagonal corners replace the standard rounded border, 13 cm
excerpt: The hexagon variant of the African flower changes the border construction so that each of the six corners forms a pointed tip rather than a rounded ch-2 space. The result is a true geometric hexagon that tiles without gaps in a flat grid, making it the joining-friendly choice for throws where the motifs sit edge to edge.
sourceNotes: Synthesised from the African flower construction with hexagonal border modification. Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 6 (1891), hexagonal motif section (Internet Archive).
heroPrompt: An African flower hexagon crochet motif in coral petals, cream centre, and mustard border with pointed hexagonal corners, photographed flat on natural linen in soft daylight. 13 cm, true hexagon shape visible.

chartDefinition.title: African flower hexagon variant
chartDefinition.caption: Three rounds. A: dc ring. B: nine puff petals. C: hexagonal border with (2tr, ch 3, 2tr) pointed corners at six tips.

glossaryTerms.definition: Several elongated half trebles drawn together at the top. Forms the nine petals in round 2.
Joining motifs during the final border round by replacing a chain with a slip stitch into the matched corner of the adjacent tile.

content.text: The hexagon variant of the African flower keeps the

petal construction of rounds 1 and 2 but changes the border chain at each corner from ch-2 (rounded) to ch-3 (pointed). The single extra chain at each of the six corners produces the pointed tip of a regular hexagon. When these motifs sit edge to edge in a grid the pointed corners interlock, leaving a very narrow gap — much smaller than the gap between rounded-corner versions.
Three colours give the clearest read: centre, petals, and border. Two colours also work, omitting the colour change before round 3.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 3 g Colour A, 5 g Colour B, 6 g Colour C — all DK-weight cotton. A 4 mm crochet hook. Tapestry needle. Scissors. Blocking mat and pins.

content.text: Each finished hexagon variant measures 13 cm flat side to flat side in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook, after a steam-block.
chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st) — UK and US shared.
puff stitch (puff) — three elongated half trebles drawn together.
Work rounds 1 and 2 exactly as the three-colour African flower. At the end of round 2: 9 puff petals, 9 sl-st gaps.

Join Colour C at any sl-st gap between petals. Ch 3 (counts as first tr). Work 1 more tr into same gap. Ch 1. *Into top of next puff work (2tr, ch 3, 2tr) — pointed corner made. Ch 1. Work 2tr into next sl-st gap. Ch 1.* Repeat from * to * four more times. Into last puff top work (2tr, ch 3, 2tr). Ch 1. Sl st to top of beg ch-3 to join. (48 tr, 6 ch-3 pointed corners, 12 ch-1 side spaces.) Fasten off.

definition.title: African flower hexagon variant
definition.caption: Rounds 1 and 2 as standard African flower. Round 3 uses ch-3 pointed corners instead of ch-2.

content.text: Fasten off and weave in all ends. Steam-block with pins at each of the six ch-3 corner tips to set the pointed hexagonal shape.
on round 3, replacing each ch-3 joining corner with ch-1, sl st through the matched corner of the adjacent tile, ch-1. This produces an invisible join at each hexagonal tip.
Handwash in cool water with mild soap, or machine-wash on a wool cycle. Lay flat to dry.

Fill the six gaps that appear between hexagons in a honeycomb grid with a small three-round triangle motif worked in the border colour. The daisy motif (crochet-daisy-basic) uses a similar petal construction to the African flower but produces a flat circular shape rather than a hexagon.
